title: TSMC Stock (TSM) Falls 10.8% as Chip Stocks Slide (Nov 5)
summary: TSMC stock (TSM) fell 10.78% to $353.10 on Nov 5 as chip stocks slid for a second day after Democrats' midterm wins stirred AI spending fears.
body_markdown:
After the decline, TSM sits 27.56% below its 52-week high and 32.34% above its 52-week low.


## Why TSMC Stock Fell


The drop did not come from company news:[TIKR](https://finance.yahoo.com/markets/stocks/articles/tsmc-sinks-10-umc-down-182304636.html) reported that TSMC had no news of its own on Thursday. Financial media tied the fall instead to a chip rout that deepened after Democrats' larger-than-expected midterm wins raised fears of a slower AI build-out.


Two industry reports added pressure, as reported by TIKR. Qualcomm, a TSMC customer,[warned on memory costs after Wednesday's close](https://www.heygotrade.com/en/news/chip-earnings-selloff-qualcomm-arm-marvell/) , and Bloomberg reported on Thursday morning that Micron had paused a $4.5 billion Taiwan plant.


The selling also reflects wider doubts about AI budgets. According to[The Motley Fool](https://finance.yahoo.com/markets/stocks/articles/advanced-micro-devices-vs-taiwan-202002562.html) , recent selling pressure has raised questions about the sustainability of massive AI infrastructure spending.


## TSM Stock Analysis: Supporting Factors and Risks


### Supporting Factors


- According to the company's official[third-quarter release](https://pr.tsmc.com/english/news/3346) , TSMC's revenue rose 41.2% from a year earlier to US$46.72 billion, with a 66.4% gross margin and diluted EPS of NT$29.43, or US$4.60 per ADR unit.
- The same release guides fourth-quarter revenue to US$52.3 billion to US$54.3 billion, with a gross margin of 65% to 67%.
- The Motley Fool reported that TSMC generated roughly $32 billion in free cash flow in 2025 even after more than $40 billion in capital expenditures, with a debt-to-equity ratio of about 0.2x.


### Risks


- TIKR wrote that if AI spending does slow, TSMC's 2027 guidance in mid-January will be the first sign.
- The Motley Fool lists heavy capital requirements and competition from rival chipmakers among the risks to the business.
- The same article flags geopolitical risk from TSMC's manufacturing being concentrated in Taiwan amid tensions with China.


The next read on demand is TSMC's October revenue, which TIKR says is due next week and will be the first check on the fourth-quarter guidance.
